profile.reading:
This is CSC IT Center for Science's data centre in Kajaani, in the Kainuu region of central Finland, built inside a converted former UPM-Kymmene paper mill warehouse at the Renforsin Ranta business park. The OpenStreetMap point was originally created under the name CSC Kajaani data center before being renamed to the organisation's own name. CSC has operated on the site since 2012, and the brownfield reuse of an existing industrial hall was a deliberate choice that cut the carbon cost of construction as well as the schedule. The Finnish architecture and engineering firm Sweco handled the conversion of the roughly 200 metre long building, whose renovated facade combines corrugated steel panels in several colours with CorTen weathering steel, chosen to echo the red brick industrial architecture of the surrounding area.

CSC is a Finnish non-profit limited company with a special mission, owned by the Finnish state and by Finnish higher education institutions and administered under the Ministry of Education and Culture. It was established in 1971, is headquartered in Espoo, and supplies supercomputing, cloud, quantum computing, data storage, digital preservation and archival services to universities and research institutes across Finland. It also runs Funet, the national research and education network.

The Kajaani building hosts Finland's national supercomputer Roihu and the pan-European supercomputer LUMI, which CSC operates on behalf of the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking and which this registry also tracks as its own separate facility. It additionally houses the large data management system of EUMETSAT, the European organisation for the exploitation of meteorological satellites, supporting the European Union's Destination Earth initiative. The site is expanding to take the next pan-European system, LUMI-AI, and the LUMI-IQ quantum computer, both part of the LUMI AI Factory, with the expansion expected to be completed in 2027 and the machines arriving after that. CSC's ISO/IEC 27001 certified information security management system covers the Kajaani centre.

On energy, CSC and the LUMI programme publish more than most operators. The wider data centre area has ready built electrical infrastructure of up to 230 megawatts with an on-site national grid connection and access to hundreds of megawatts more, which is site electrical service capacity rather than IT load, and no IT load figure for the building is published. Electricity is renewable and backed by guarantees of origin. Kajaani's northern latitude allows efficient free air and liquid cooling all year round, and waste heat from the cooling systems is recovered and fed into the City of Kajaani's district heating network, covering the annual heating needs of hundreds of households. Excess heat is also used to warm incoming air for the building's own offices.

Kajaani has since become a data centre cluster in its own right, drawing other operators alongside teaching and research activity from Kajaani University of Applied Sciences, the University of Oulu and Kainuu Vocational College. The location is operator neutral, part of the Nordic research network, served by multiple physical connectivity routes, and positioned for the Far North Fibre project.
